scores.factor: Data model fit: document store vs relational for a financial ledger (joins, constraints, reporting)
evidence: packages/db/src/schema/_common.ts:52-59 — paise = bigint, percent = numeric(5,2), sqft = numeric(10,2) helpers used by every table
packages/db/src/schema/money.ts:40-90 — demands with partial UNIQUE(booking_id, installment_seq) WHERE status<>'VOID', CHECK demands_split_chk (cash+account=total) and non-negative CHECKs
packages/db/src/schema/bookings.ts:146-155 — bookings_agreement_split_chk (cash_agreed+account_agreed=agreement_value), one ACTIVE booking per flat partial unique
apps/api/src/modules/money/services/ledger.ts:421-462 — ledger is a per-booking projection re-derived from source tables; rebuild compares row by row (integrity finding e)
packages/db/src/schema/json.ts (FlatSnapshot.price_paise, PriceBreakupLine.amount_paise, Cancellation refund/deduction) — money still inside jsonb
packages/db/test/data-model.test.ts:1148-1261 — tests pin bigint for every *_paise column, numeric precisions, date vs timestamptz and the money CHECKs
scores.strengths: A properly relational PostgreSQL 16 model: real FKs, enums sourced from contracts, partial unique indexes that make double-booking and double-raising impossible under concurrency, and (since the hardening round) database CHECKs on the core money identities. Reports are SQL joins, and the materialised booking summary is verified against a full rebuild by the integrity report.
scores.gaps: The ledger is a single-entry, per-booking running-balance projection, not a double-entry journal (no chart of accounts, no debit/credit lines, no GL/Tally export). It is rewritten wholesale on every rebuild instead of being an append-only book of record. Money still lives in jsonb where no type or CHECK protects it: flat_snapshot.price_paise, price_breakup lines and cancellation.refund_paise/deduction_paise. Structural references are uuid[] arrays with no FK (projects/blocks.stage_sequence, flat_types.spec_item_ids). V2 top finding on missing money CHECKs is fixed (0002_foundation_hardening.sql:69-76); the jsonb-money part of that finding is not.
scores.world_best_would: Model money as a double-entry journal (immutable journal lines per booking/bucket with a GL mapping) from which the customer ledger and summaries are projections. Keep every amount in typed bigint columns (price_breakup_lines, cancellation columns) and use join tables with FKs for stage sequences and spec items.

scores.factor: Referential integrity & constraints (foreign keys, unique constraints, orphan prevention, usage checks before deactivate)
evidence: packages/db/drizzle/0002_foundation_hardening.sql:63-76 — CHECKs: bookings split/non-negative, demands split/non-negative, other charges total=amount+GST, flat/parking prices ≥ 0
packages/db/src/schema/customers.ts:80-85 — partial UNIQUE (company_id, phone) and (company_id, pan_hash) WHERE erased_at IS NULL
apps/api/src/modules/masters/factory.ts:299-308 — deactivate returns 409 IN_USE with usage_count/used_by; kinds.ts:202-711 usage queries incl. jsonb containment
packages/db/src/schema/inventory.ts:329-332,369 — flats.rate_card_id, flats.booking_id, flats.hold_by_user_id, parking_slots.booking_id are bare uuids with no FK

drizzle/meta/0004_snapshot.json (my analysis) — 44 FK columns have no index leading on them, e.g. payments.customer_id, demands.customer_id, leads.customer_id, service_requests.booking_id, flats.flat_type_id
scores.strengths: Almost every relationship is a real FK, and cascades are limited to true child rows. Business invariants are partial unique indexes enforced under concurrency. The money identities and live-customer dedupe are now database-enforced, and every master kind blocks deactivation while it is in use, including references held inside jsonb (GIN-backed containment).
scores.gaps: Deliberate soft references remain with no FK: flats.booking_id/rate_card_id/hold_by_user_id, parking_slots.booking_id, bookings.price_deviation_by/plan_acceptance_document_id, every *_by column, the polymorphic documents/notifications/audit entity_id, uuid[] arrays, and ids embedded in jsonb. No composite (company_id, id) FKs exist, so a child row's company_id can diverge from its parent's. There is no CHECK that demands.paid_paise ≤ total or that other-charge paid ≤ total, and no range CHECK on percents or phone format. 44 FK columns have no supporting index, so every FK check on delete and every usage count (e.g. flats by flat_type_id, payments by payment_mode_id) is a sequential scan. V2 top finding (no money CHECKs, no unique dedupe indexes) is fixed; the concurrent duplicate-customer test now exists (crm-adversarial.test.ts:194).
scores.world_best_would: Give every reference an FK, using deferrable FKs to break cycles (flats↔bookings) and link tables in place of uuid[] and polymorphic ids. Add composite tenant FKs, paid ≤ total CHECKs and an index on every FK column, and add a CI test that fails on any unindexed FK.

scores.factor: Indexing strategy & query efficiency (compound indexes vs actual query shapes, regex search without index, count_documents on every page)
evidence: packages/db/drizzle/0002_foundation_hardening.sql:21-55 — trigram GIN on customers/leads/users/bookings/flats/projects/blocks/payments/service_requests columns, (company_id, sort DESC, id DESC) indexes; duplicate ledger index dropped
apps/api/src/lib/list.ts:60-66 — COUNT_ESTIMATE_ABOVE 10,000 with planner estimate; keyset cursors with microsecond keys

apps/api/src/modules/money/routes/payments.ts:178-186 and :379-385 — payments/demands search OR across joined tables plus instrument->>'number', demands.demand_number and installment_name, none trigram-indexed
apps/api/src/modules/audit/index.ts:75-77, web/visitRoutes.ts:145 — audit_logs and site_visits ILIKE search columns have no trigram index
apps/api/src/modules/crm/customers.ts:126-171 — customer 360 filters payments by customer_id and counts them, and filters leads by customer_id; none of these columns is indexed

docs/PERFORMANCE.md 'Run 2026-10-26T17:45' and '17:53' — at 200 connections p95 is /flats 333 ms and /bookings 304 ms, the rest under 300 ms; at 1,000 connections every list misses (670–1,411 ms) and only /dashboard (265 ms) and /public/projects (125 ms) meet 300 ms; seed is 130 flats and 10 bookings
scores.strengths: Default list sorts have matching compound indexes, the main contains-searches now use pg_trgm GIN, and counts switch to planner estimates above 10k rows (skipped entirely for a non-full search page). Statements are prepared and compiled once, and keyset cursors avoid deep OFFSET. A db test proves the planner uses the trigram and sort indexes.
scores.gaps: Several search shapes still cannot use an index: bookings, payments and demands OR their search term across joined tables (booking number, customer name, flat number) and the unindexed instrument->>'number'. demands.demand_number, site_visits name/phone, audit_logs action/actor_name/entity_id::text and login_events are searched with ILIKE '%…%' and have no trigram index, so they seq-scan on the largest append-only tables. 44 FK columns are unindexed, including hot customer-360 lookups (payments.customer_id, leads.customer_id). Trigram cannot help terms under 3 characters. Every load number comes from a 130-flat / 10-booking seed (plus one 200k-customer EXPLAIN), so the V2 finding asking for a synthetic 5-lakh-customer load test is still open. The other parts of that finding (trigram, partition scripts, duplicate ledger index) are fixed.
scores.world_best_would: Derive the required index set from the actual route query shapes in a test: put a denormalised search document (tsvector or trigram) on each list's root table instead of cross-join ORs, and index every FK. Validate plans and p95 on a synthetic production-scale dataset (5 lakh customers, crores of ledger and audit rows) in CI.

scores.factor: Money representation & rounding (integer paise, ROUND_HALF_UP, telescoping to exact 100%, float leakage in API inputs/prices)
evidence: packages/domain/src/money.ts:35-44,96-150 — divRoundHalfUp on BigInt, digit-wise scaleDecimal, basis-point pctOfPaise/bpOfPaise, mulPaiseBySqft
packages/domain/src/dues.ts:163-196 — telescoping installmentAmounts so demands sum exactly to the agreed amount per bucket
packages/contracts/src/common.ts:16-43 — int-only PaiseSchema; PercentSchema uses float hasMaxDecimals with 1e-6 tolerance
packages/contracts/src/modules/rateCards.ts:34-45 — PERCENT PLC value has no ≤2-decimal check; verified that 2.555 passes the contract while domain toBasisPoints throws MoneyError
packages/db/src/schema/inventory.ts:431 — rate_card_plc_rules.value numeric(14,4) read as a JS float, holding paise or percent depending on calc_mode
packages/db/src/client.ts:164 — bigint parsed with Number(v): no range check at the driver boundary
scores.strengths: Money is integer paise end to end: bigint columns, int-only wire schemas, BigInt half-up rounding and basis-point percents. Telescoping is exact to the paise in both buckets, and agreement revisions and ledger rebuilds reuse the same rounding functions. The hardening round added database CHECKs so splits must sum and amounts can never be negative.
scores.gaps: Percent and sqft inputs are JS floats checked with a 1e-6 epsilon. A PERCENT PLC with three decimals passes the contract and is stored in numeric(14,4), then throws MoneyError at pricing time: a 500, not a 422. The PLC column mixes paise and percent semantics and allows fractional paise. bigint values cross the driver through Number() with no overflow guard (theoretical at builder scale, but not bank-grade). Derived per-sqft rates use float division plus Math.round (inventory/flats.ts:492, reports/salesReports.ts:226,235), and cancellation money sits in jsonb.
scores.world_best_would: Carry percents as integer basis points or decimal strings on the wire, split PLC values into a bigint paise column and a basis-points column, and read bigint as BigInt or string with explicit range checks. Then no float ever touches a stored or validated money figure.

scores.factor: Canonical forms / normalisation (phone E.164, PAN uppercase, hashes for dedupe, denormalised copies kept in sync)
evidence: packages/contracts/src/common.ts:64-115 — PhoneSchema → 10-digit Indian national form; PAN/IFSC/GSTIN upperTrim; email lowerTrim; Aadhaar stripSpaces
apps/api/src/lib/crypto.ts:78-80 and crm/customerService.ts:83-99 — AES ciphertext + HMAC keyed hash + last4 for PAN/Aadhaar
packages/db/src/schema/customers.ts:80-85 — dedupe enforced by partial unique indexes on (company_id, phone) / (company_id, pan_hash)
apps/api/src/modules/masters/kinds.ts:433-578 — flatTypesKind has no afterWrite, so flats.flat_type_code (inventory.ts:317) goes stale when a flat type's code is edited
packages/db/src/schema/customers.ts:100-115 — co_applicants keep pan_hash but no aadhaar_hash; customers.email is text, not citext
apps/api/src/modules/inventory/service.ts:168-222 — unit_counts recomputed from flats in one statement (not incremented)
scores.strengths: Identifiers are canonicalised at the schema edge, and PAN/Aadhaar are encrypted with keyed HMAC hashes for dedupe. The dedupe is now backed by database unique indexes as well as advisory locks. Money-relevant materialised copies (booking summary, unit counts, portal phone) are recomputed inside the same transaction and checked by the nightly integrity report.
scores.gaps: Phones are stored in 10-digit national form, not E.164, so NRI buyers (a meaningful segment for Indian builders) cannot be recorded at all. No database CHECK enforces any canonical format, so any path that bypasses Zod can store non-canonical phone, PAN or email. flats.flat_type_code is a denormalised copy that is never re-synced when the master code changes. Co-applicant Aadhaar has no hash, so its duplicates are undetectable, and customers.email is plain text while users.email is citext. HASH_KEY rotation would silently break every dedupe hash.
scores.world_best_would: Store E.164 plus a national display form, with CHECK constraints for canonical shapes. Hash every encrypted identifier uniformly with a versioned key so it can be rehashed on rotation. Keep denormalised codes in sync via a trigger or a master afterWrite.

scores.factor: Snapshotting & versioning of structural data (flat snapshots, plan snapshots, stage snapshots) and consistency after master edits
evidence: apps/api/src/modules/money/services/bookings.ts:295-330 — booking stores flat_snapshot (rooms, areas, price, breakup), plan_snapshot and list_price_paise
apps/api/src/modules/inventory/flats.ts:588-668 — flat-type change re-snapshots rooms/areas (optional reprice) only while AVAILABLE, audited
apps/api/src/modules/masters/kinds.ts:851-874 — payment-plan edit DELETEs and re-INSERTs installments (no plan version row) but now asserts fit with active assignments
apps/api/src/modules/money/services/bookings.ts:552-570 — agreement revision UPDATEs posted demands' amounts in place (history only in agreement_revisions + audit)
apps/api/src/modules/portal/common.ts:77 and portal/bookings.ts:366-379 — portal reads flatTypes.specItemIds live, so spec edits leak into sold flats
apps/api/src/modules/money/services/integrity.ts:96-231 — integrity report checks demands against the plan snapshot and the summary against a rebuild
scores.strengths: All three snapshot levels the spec asks for exist and are guarded: flats at generation, towers' stage records, and bookings' flat and plan snapshots. Agreement and plan changes are append-only revision rows with before/after snapshots. Rate-card apply reprices only Available flats, with dry-run and per-flat audit, and plan edits are now validated against active tower assignments.
scores.gaps: Masters have no version history: plan installments are replaced by DELETE+INSERT, and flat types and stages are edited in place, so the only record of an earlier version is the audit JSON. Nothing flags a snapshot that differs from its master, and there is no bulk 're-snapshot Available flats from master' action, so unsold flats silently keep old areas after a master edit. Specification items are not in the booking snapshot. Posted demands are mutated in place on agreement revision. Snapshots are unversioned jsonb with no schema-version field and no DB-side validation.
scores.world_best_would: Version masters (plan_versions, flat_type_versions) and point every snapshot at a version id with a schema version. Surface a 'stale vs master' flag with an audited apply-to-Available action. Snapshot every buyer-visible attribute, including specifications.

scores.factor: Migrations & schema evolution (migrate_phase7, dual-field legacy handling milestone_* vs installment_*)
evidence: packages/db/src/migrate.ts:58-69 — migrations under a session advisory lock (MIGRATION_LOCK_KEY), then idempotent src/sql/*.sql

packages/db/drizzle/meta/_journal.json and 0000–0004 — committed drizzle-kit SQL chain with snapshots; 0002 hand-written backfills tested on existing data (packages/db/test/hardening.test.ts:334, :427)
docker-compose.yml:9,30-31,105 — one-shot migrate service before 2 API replicas; RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_BOOT=false (V2 first-boot race fixed)
packages/db/drizzle/0002_foundation_hardening.sql:39-76 — ~20 GIN/btree indexes created non-CONCURRENTLY and CHECKs added without NOT VALID inside the migration transaction
packages/db/src/sql/0001_triggers.sql:57-75 — every deploy DROPs and re-CREATEs set_updated_at on every table (an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock per table)
packages/db/test/data-model.test.ts:1095 — Drizzle↔DB column drift test; .github/workflows/ci.yml has no drizzle-kit check
scores.strengths: Schema evolution is a committed, journaled SQL chain with an idempotent trigger layer, serialised across replicas by an advisory lock and run by a dedicated owner-role migrate job before the app starts. Data backfills and the ledger re-ordering migration (LEDGER_REBUILD) are tested on existing data. The greenfield design avoids v1's milestone_*/installment_* dual-field debt entirely.
scores.gaps: There are no down migrations and no written expand/contract policy; rollback means a full restore. Migrations run in one transaction, so indexes cannot be built CONCURRENTLY and CHECKs are added without NOT VALID/VALIDATE: on lakh- or crore-row tables, 0002-style migrations would block writes for the whole build. The trigger file re-locks every table at every deploy. CI has no drizzle-kit check for type, default or index drift; only column names are tested. No v1 (Mongo) importer exists, so a live builder has no cut-over path.
scores.world_best_would: Adopt expand/contract migrations with online DDL (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside the transaction, NOT VALID then VALIDATE, batched backfills), a CI drift gate and rehearsed down/forward-fix scripts. Ship a tested, idempotent v1→v2 importer with a dry-run reconciliation report.

scores.factor: Soft delete / audit immutability (can audit be edited? are financial records ever deleted? ledger_entries delete_many + insert_many rebuild)
evidence: packages/db/src/sql/0001_triggers.sql:7-44 — audit_logs raises on UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE; payments and demands raise on DELETE; lines 24-26 say ledger_entries is deliberately unguarded
infra/postgres/init/01-roles.sql:16,49 — the API runs as NOSUPERUSER kkt_app with TRUNCATE/TRIGGER revoked (V2 superuser finding fixed)

apps/api/src/modules/money/services/ledger.ts:458-461 — rebuild(write) DELETEs every ledger row of the booking and re-INSERTs; called on agreement revision (bookings.ts:580), plan change (:673), stage undo (dues.ts:544), integrity repair and LEDGER_REBUILD
apps/api/src/modules/money/services/ledger.ts:331 — the rebuild excludes VOID demands, so a voided demand disappears from the ledger with no compensating row

My check on kkt_audit3_b: the only guard triggers are on audit_logs, demands and payments; inside a rolled-back transaction, UPDATE payments SET amount_paise=amount_paise+100 on a CLEARED receipt and DELETE FROM ledger_entries both succeeded
scores.strengths: The audit log is immutable at the database level, including TRUNCATE. The application role now cannot truncate, disable triggers or act as owner, so the guards bind the application itself. Payments and demands are never deleted (reverse/void with a mandatory reason), and masters and documents are soft-deleted with usage checks.
scores.gaps: The V2 finding asking for a rebuild-epoch ledger is not fixed: ledger_entries has no guard, and agreement revisions, plan changes, stage undos and repairs routinely DELETE+INSERT the whole ledger without keeping the prior rows. Voided demands vanish from the customer ledger instead of producing a reversal row. Posted demands' amounts are UPDATEd in place, and no column-level guard stops the app role from changing a cleared payment's amount, booking or bucket; only the nightly integrity report would notice. bookings, booking_other_charges (which cascade from bookings), agreement_revisions, booking_plan_revisions and contra_entries have no delete guard, and the audit log has no tamper-evidence (hash chain/WORM).
scores.world_best_would: Make the ledger an append-only journal: corrections as compensating entries, rebuilds as a new epoch that supersedes rather than deletes, and DEMAND_VOID rows. Freeze financial columns after posting with triggers, guard every financial table against DELETE and TRUNCATE, and hash-chain the audit log to WORM storage.

scores.factor: Backup, restore, right-to-erasure
evidence: docker-compose.prod.yml:68-70 and infra/backup/backup.sh:1-80 — WAL archiving (RPO ≤ 5 min), weekly base backups, nightly pg_dump + sha256, automated restore drill into a scratch DB, retention, off-site hook, status.prom + KktBackupStale alert
apps/api/src/modules/admin/backup.ts:377-403 — tenant-scoped export in one REPEATABLE READ snapshot via server-side cursor (no row cap), manifest with sha256 and FK load order
apps/api/test/integration/backup-restore.test.ts — I ran it: 3/3 passed (exact-value round trip, clean integrity report, tamper and stripped-backup refusal, CLI restore)

apps/api/src/modules/admin/erase.ts:1-6,98-262 — single erasure path (crm/customers.ts:835-839 delegates) anonymising customer, co-applicants, portal, documents (bytes removed), leads, visits, enquiries, login_events (:250), testimonials

apps/api/src/modules/crm/customerService.ts:600-608 — customer.create audit stores the full customer view (name, phone, email, DOB, addresses, nominee), which immutable audit_logs keep forever after erasure
apps/erp/src/features/crm/customer/EraseCustomerDialog.tsx:36 and apps/erp/src/features/system/api.ts:126 — erasure and backups reachable from the ERP (V2 finding fixed)
scores.strengths: V2 top findings 2 and 3 are largely fixed. Continuous WAL archiving with PITR, nightly dumps with an automated restore drill and staleness alerting, and an uncapped, checksummed, tenant-scoped application export with a tested restore CLI. Erasure is now one implementation, reachable from the ERP, that scrubs every operational copy of the PII while keeping financial rows.
scores.gaps: Erasure is still incomplete for DPDP: the immutable audit_logs before/after (customer.create/update hold full contact details), service_request_messages.author_name and ticket text keep the PII, and there is no crypto-shredding design. Storage deletion is best-effort with no retry queue (erase.ts:300-312). Dumps, base backups and WAL are written unencrypted, and the 14 days of retained backups re-contain erased PII. RESTORE.md states the Compose wrappers were never executed (no Docker), so the RTO figures are estimates. There is no customer-initiated export or erasure request flow.
scores.world_best_would: Keep audit and other immutable PII in an encrypted side column under a per-customer key, so that erasure is a key shred that also propagates to backups. Encrypt backups at rest and off-site, retry storage deletions from a durable queue, and offer a tracked self-service data-principal request flow with a regularly executed, timed restore drill.

scores.factor: Multi-tenancy readiness (company_id on every query? unique indexes scoped by company? cross-tenant leaks)
evidence: packages/db/test/data-model.test.ts:1199 — every business table has company_id uuid NOT NULL referencing companies; business-key uniques and sequences are company-scoped (identity.ts sequences PK, users_company_email_uq)
apps/api/src/modules/money/common.ts:84-101, search/index.ts:88-109, reports/services/dashboards.ts:90-93 — loaders, search and cache keys filter by companyId
apps/api/src/modules/auth/staff.ts:153 and auth/portal.ts:92 — login looks up users.email / portal_users.phone with no company, although uniqueness is per company
apps/api/src/modules/web/shared.ts:141 — the public site serves the first-created company; packages/db/src/schema/inventory.ts:169 — website slug UNIQUE is global

apps/api/src/modules/admin/tools.ts:527 — job_runs (no company_id) readable by any tenant's admin; login_events.company_id nullable (identity.ts:156); idempotency_keys/job_runs exported unscoped (integrate-crosscut.md)
packages/db/src/schema (snapshot analysis) — no RLS, no composite (company_id, id) FKs; company_id does not lead any index on ledger_entries, notifications, documents, block_stages and other tables
scores.strengths: The data layer is tenant-shaped as the spec requires: company_id NOT NULL on every business table (test-enforced), company-scoped business keys and numbering, and company filters in the central loaders, search and dashboard caches. Backups and documents have two-company isolation tests.
scores.gaps: The V2 multi-tenancy findings are unfixed apart from the bootstrap race. Staff and portal login still resolve credentials without a company, so two tenants sharing an email or phone would log into an arbitrary row. The public website and its cache are bound to the first company, and slugs are global. Job runs, idempotency keys and the public cache version are global, and login_events.company_id is nullable. There is no Postgres RLS or tenant GUC as a second line of defence and no composite FK ensuring children share their parent's company. Cross-tenant tests cover only a few modules, not every route.
scores.world_best_would: Resolve the tenant from host or company code before any credential lookup and make every identifier lookup (company_id, identifier). Enable RLS with a per-transaction tenant GUC, use composite tenant FKs, and scope public caches, slugs, jobs and idempotency per tenant. Add a generated two-tenant conformance suite that calls every registered route with foreign ids and expects 404.

scores.factor: 1. Service architecture & modularity (routers/services/domain separation, coupling, cyclic imports)
evidence: eslint.config.mjs:15-49,129-133 kkt/module-boundaries is an error: a module may import another business module only through its index.ts (fixes the V2 finding that construction/admin imported money/services/*.js directly)
My scan of 166 files / 811 value-import edges under apps/api/src found 0 cycles; the module graph is acyclic (portal -> construction, documents, money, reports, service; reports -> documents, money)

apps/api/src/modules/money/index.ts:16-122 re-exports about 80 symbols, including internal lock helpers (lockBooking, lockFlatAndBlockOf), SQL select fragments (DEMAND_SELECT, demandJoins) and moneyTransaction, so the 'public surface' is most of the module

apps/api/src/modules/inventory/blocks.ts:305 registerBlockRoutes is 869 lines with 17 inline queries and 4 transactions (it was 368 lines in V2); crm/leads.ts:106 leadRoutes is 644 lines; users/index.ts holds the routes, SQL and rules in one 551-line file

apps/api/src/modules/masters/kinds.ts:104 (a core module) imports assertPlanFitsActiveAssignments from the auto-discovered money module; apps/api/src/jobs/alerts.ts:10 (core) imports ../modules/notifications/service.js, past the index and outside the lint rule's reach

apps/api/src/worker.ts:394-401 now builds the full app before consuming jobs, so job handlers exist in the standalone worker; they are still registered as a side effect of Fastify plugin registration (money/index.ts:130, web/visitRoutes.ts:545 at import time)
scores.strengths: Clean package layering (contracts, domain with zero dependencies, db, api), a module loader, a route() helper that makes guards mechanically checkable, and a lint-enforced module-boundary rule. There are no import cycles. The money module is properly layered into routes, services, views and common.
scores.gaps: Layering is consistent only in money. Inventory, crm, users, web and portal route files hold SQL, transactions and business rules inside handlers, and the largest registration functions grew after hardening. The boundary rule only checks relative import paths: it does not limit how wide an index's re-export surface is, it does not cover lib/, jobs/ or plugins/ importing module internals, and it does not stop a core module depending on a pluggable one (masters -> money). Job registration happens as a side effect of plugin registration (a process-global Map), which couples the worker topology to HTTP plugin wiring. The idempotency plugin installing the version policy (plugins/idempotency.ts:150) is another cross-concern coupling.
scores.world_best_would: Give every module the same thin-route, service and repository layering, with narrow index exports checked by a dependency-cruiser style rule that also covers lib, jobs and plugins. Register jobs from a declarative per-module manifest independent of Fastify, and keep core modules free of dependencies on optional ones.

scores.strengths: Token design is solid: 15-minute EdDSA access tokens with audience separation, opaque hashed refresh families with atomic rotation and reuse detection, and argon2id (64 MiB, t=3). Every session event is audited. The V2 findings are fixed in code: attempts_left is gone, unknown identifiers get identical 401/423 answers and the same argon2 cost, lockout is per (identifier, IP) with a separate account-wide threshold, the MFA step is IP-bound, and keys rotate through a kid ring.
scores.gaps: Forced MFA still depends on role names (plugins/auth.ts:36,345), so a custom role holding every sensitive permission escapes it, which repeats a V2 gap. TOTP codes can be replayed inside the ±1 window (staff.ts:52, no last-used step stored); there are no recovery codes and no WebAuthn; enrolment only needs a stolen access token, so an attacker can bind their own authenticator to the account. Sessions slide forever because each refresh grants another 7 days, and there is no idle timeout or new-device alert. The password policy (password.ts:163-171) has no breached-password or common-password check, the portal has no second factor, the in-flight burst guard is per process (about 5×N guesses with N workers), and 20 failures from four IPs can still lock any account for 15 minutes.
scores.world_best_would: It would require MFA by permission sensitivity rather than role name, using WebAuthn or passkeys with recovery codes and TOTP replay protection, and step-up re-authentication for MFA and credential changes. It would add breached-password screening, an absolute session lifetime, idle timeout, new-device notification and a cross-instance attempt budget. For hard account locks it would use risk-based challenges (CAPTCHA or OTP) instead.

scores.factor: Field-level encryption, masking, audited reveal (crypto.py Fernet, pan_hash HMAC, reveal logging)
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/crypto.ts:23-68 (AES-256-GCM, 12-byte IV, `<kid>.<iv>.<tag>.<ct>`, multi-key ring, no AAD)

scores.strengths: PAN, Aadhaar, customer and company bank accounts, and TOTP secrets are encrypted with authenticated encryption under a kid-tagged key ring. A tested re-encryption job uses compare-and-set to avoid lost updates. Keyed hashes plus partial unique indexes give dedupe without plaintext. Reveals and sensitive-file links are permission-gated and audited, and KYC follows a maker-checker workflow.
scores.gaps: There is no KMS, HSM or envelope encryption: data keys are a SHA-256 of environment strings (crypto.ts:5-7). Ciphertexts carry no AAD binding them to row or column, so a value can be moved between rows undetected. List endpoints decrypt every PAN and Aadhaar just to mask them although last4 is stored (customerService.ts:118-127), which widens plaintext exposure and costs CPU. HASH_KEY cannot be rotated. Uploaded KYC scans are not encrypted at the application layer, and no explicit S3 SSE or KMS is set. A reveal is all-or-nothing (PAN, Aadhaar, bank account and every co-applicant), records no reason and has no rate limit or anomaly alert. Full Aadhaar storage is not in a UIDAI-style Aadhaar Data Vault, and audit snapshots keep PII after erasure.
scores.world_best_would: It would use KMS-backed envelope encryption with per-field AAD and Aadhaar tokenised in a vault. Masks would come from last4 without decrypting, and reveals would be per field with a justification, rate limits and anomaly alerts. KYC files would be encrypted with per-object keys, and the HMAC key would rotate on a versioned scheme.

No user-controlled regex exists (the only dynamic RegExps, at admin/tools.ts:196 and documents/exports.ts:109, build on internal keys). Mongo-style operator injection does not apply to this design. Postgres data-exception codes (22xxx) would map to 400, cursors would be signed, and lint rules would ban sql.raw or unsafe outside an allow-listed module.

Image resizing and storage I/O happen synchronously inside the request's DB transaction, lengthening lock time under load. There is no malware scanning, document versioning or share expiry.
scores.world_best_would: Run business-hours SLA clocks with pause/resume and escalation tiers, and push notifications over SSE/WebSocket and mobile push with per-user preferences and digests. Move media processing to an async pipeline after commit, with AV scanning, versioned documents and expiring shares.

adjusted.factor: 7. Background jobs & scheduling robustness
adjusted.reason: The V2 findings are fixed. runJob rethrows so BullMQ can retry, and the final attempt raises an alert (jobs/index.ts:270-326). Jobs get 3 attempts with backoff (defaultJobOptions). But the poison-booking defect is real and is money-critical. runDailyDues (dues.ts:353-371) loops over every ACTIVE booking across all companies, with no try/catch around each moneyTransaction. There is no unhandledRejection hook and no worker health port. These outweigh the fixes more than the first auditor allowed.
